# Version Skip Validation

Whether projects measure N-1 only or N-2+ upgrade paths.

## Kubernetes Version Skew Policy

The official policy defines maximum version skew between components [42]:

| Component Pair | Maximum Skew | Changed In |
|---|---|---|
| kube-apiserver HA instances | 1 minor | — |
| kubelet → kube-apiserver | N-3 (was N-2) | v1.25 [48] |
| kube-proxy → kube-apiserver | N-3 (was N-2) | v1.25 [48] |
| controller-manager → kube-apiserver | N-1 | — |
| kube-scheduler → kube-apiserver | N-1 | — |
| kubectl → kube-apiserver | ±1 | — |

Control plane upgrades must be sequential — one minor version at a time. This is enforced by all major platforms [42].

## Cloud Provider Policies

| Platform | Control Plane Skip | Node Pool Skip | Version Support |
|---|---|---|---|
| AKS | Not allowed [21] | N-2 behind CP | N-2 (3 GA versions) |
| EKS | Not allowed [24] | N-3 from v1.28 | 14 months standard |
| GKE | Not allowed [25] | N-2 behind CP | — |
| GKE Distributed Cloud | Not allowed | Allowed (v1.29+) [46] | Reduces upgrade frequency 4→8 months |

GKE Distributed Cloud is the only platform that officially supports node pool version skipping [46].

## OpenShift Extended Update Support (EUS)

EUS releases are even-numbered minors starting with 4.12: **4.12, 4.14, 4.16** [43].

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Support extension | 14 months beyond Full Support [43] |
| Upgrade path | Must go through intermediate versions (e.g., 4.12→4.13→4.14) [44] |
| Worker optimization | MCPs can be paused to reduce reboots [44] |
| Versions NOT skipped | Control plane and operators still traverse every version [44] |

70% of reschedulable pods are moved more than necessary during sequential upgrades — the EUS worker MCP pause optimization addresses this [44].

## OLM Operator Upgrade Graph

OLM provides three mechanisms for version management [63]:

| Mechanism | Behavior | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `replaces` | Linear chain, one version at a time | Safe, predictable |
| `skips` | Direct upgrade skipping specific versions | Skipped versions become uninstallable |
| `skipRange` | Semantic version range (e.g., ">=1.0.0 <1.0.3") | **Prunes skipped versions from graph entirely** |

"OLM will never upgrade to a version that is skipped by something else" [63].

## KEP-4330: Future Skip-Level Upgrades

KEP-4330 introduces `--emulation-version` and `--min-compatibility-version` flags that enable skip-level upgrades by performing stepwise emulation version changes with fewer binary upgrades [45]. This enables future capability to upgrade from e.g., 1.33 to 1.35 [29].

## Double-Jump Upgrade Pattern (Unofficial)

Documented in practitioner blogs [47]:
- Control plane upgrades sequentially: N→N+1→N+2
- Worker nodes upgrade directly: N→N+2 (leveraging kubelet N-2 skew policy)
- Requires using only GA and Beta APIs (no Alpha)
- Successfully executed in production multiple times

## Cluster API Version Support

Cluster API defines broader support matrices [discovery agent, Tier 1]:
- Management cluster: N to N-4
- Workload cluster: N to N-6

## Counter-Perspectives

**Testing is combinatorially impractical:**
- Most ISVs only test the last 3 versions of 1 distribution
- Problems discovered in production, not pre-release
- Kubernetes team cannot anticipate every use case

**Sequential requirement creates unnecessary overhead:**
- 7 clusters × 3 version jumps = 21 separate upgrade operations [discovery agent, Tier 4]
- 30+ clusters face full-week rollouts [71]
- Fresh cluster migration often preferred over sequential bumping for outdated clusters

**N-2 works despite no official support:**
- Google GKE Distributed Cloud officially supports node pool skipping [46]
- Double-jump pattern commonly practiced in managed environments [47]
- EUS deliberately chose NOT to implement version skipping despite demand [44]

## Metric Taxonomy

| Metric | Type | Measurable By |
|---|---|---|
| Version skew compliance | Binary pass/fail | Operator (kubectl) |
| kubelet version delta | Integer (N-0 to N-3) | Operator (API server) |
| OLM upgrade graph edges | Count | Vendor (catalog) |
| EUS upgrade path validation | Binary (verified/unverified) | Vendor (Cincinnati graph) |
| Cluster API version matrix | Matrix coverage | Vendor (CI) |

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published statistics on upgrade failure rates comparing sequential vs skip-version paths
- Version skew compliance is binary (compliant or not), not graduated
- OLM skipRange adoption rates are unknown — no data on what percentage of operators use it
- KEP-4330 skip-level upgrades are future capability, not current GA
- Double-jump pattern is practitioner-documented but not vendor-supported
